A1.justification: Despite the changed title and author list, both PDFs describe the same gaze-completion-based mistake-detection work. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable. The comparison includes all supplied material: v3 ends with references, while v4 includes supplementary Sections A–B.

before.justification: V3 reports original mistake-detection and gaze-estimation experiments on three datasets, fusion/scoring ablations, and an uncertainty–mistake regression analysis.

after.justification: V4 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons, a volunteer rating study, association analyses, and supplementary sensitivity and category-level results.

M1.justification: V4 drops the optional sum-fusion branch described and tested in v3 and adds an optional late-fusion combination with hand-based MoCoDAD. The principal channel-plus-correlation gaze-completion model, KL training loss and four scoring approaches retain their substance.

E1.justification: Video training and evaluation retain EPIC-Tent, HoloAssist and IndustReal and their existing tasks. V4 adds an auxiliary study in which 40 volunteers rate the difficulty of performing HoloAssist actions without looking. Its action-category breakdowns otherwise reuse existing benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: V4 Tables 2–4 add evaluated fully supervised TimeSformer and C2F baselines. The existing gaze-only TrajREC and MoCoDAD methods, now marked G, are supplemented with hand-only, combined hand/gaze and late-fusion variants. TrajREC and MoCoDAD also enter the unsupervised comparisons, where v3 compared only GLC and the proposed method.

E3.justification: V4 adds fully supervised training with frame-level mistake labels, comparisons involving different temporal contexts, and hand-versus-gaze input controls. Supplementary Sections B.2–B.3 introduce prediction-length and threshold sweeps. These expand the experimental design; the reported dataset splits, default eight-frame clips, stride of one, and ROC-AUC/best-F1 evaluation remain.

E4.justification: V4 adds analyses of difficulty, confidence and action type versus detection success, category-specific benchmark performance, prediction-length and threshold sensitivity, and comparative heatmap case studies. V3's sum-fusion ablations, uncertainty-versus-mistake regression and action-class failure-share plots are absent. The new analyses ask different questions and are not simply relocated versions of those removed.

E5.justification: Auxiliary statistical procedures change from v3's logistic regression of mistake occurrence on uncertainty, reporting coefficient 0.68 and p < 0.001, to point-biserial correlations and chi-square/Cramer's V analyses in v4 Section 4.5. Neither version reports benchmark variability across repeated runs, seed counts or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: V4 adds extensive supervised, hand-based, ensemble, category-level and sensitivity results while retaining the principal method's benchmark F1/AUC entries. For example, the new EPIC-Tent one-class ensemble reports F1 0.54 and AUC 0.72. Retained results also change: gaze-completion F1 values of 0.40/0.43 in v3 Table 2 become 0.38/0.40 in v4 supplementary Table 1, and gaze-only EPIC-Tent TrajREC F1 changes from 0.45 to 0.40. These revisions do not establish same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The formal problem setup and mathematical scoring rules retain their substance. V4 abbreviates the explicit DTW alignment expression and spells out the standard KL loss already used in v3. These are explanatory changes rather than new theoretical results, proofs or substantive mathematical assumptions.

C1.justification: V4's abstract and introduction foreground skilled activities and add claims about matching supervised performance and being particularly effective for complex, low-confidence, hand-eye-coordination and object-manipulation actions. Supervised parity is demonstrated most directly by the EPIC-Tent one-class ensemble's AUC of 0.72 in Table 2. The original gaze-completion contributions and HoloAssist challenge-ranking claim remain.

C2.justification: V4 adds substantive explanations concerning novice users, action complexity, complementary hand/gaze information and weaker performance on preparation or inspection actions. It removes v3's explicit limitation concerning key-step-ordering mistakes. Some new interpretations are inconsistent: Section 4.5 alternates between higher and lower confidence, and supplementary B.1 attributes an inspection/verification result to task preparation.

D1.justification: V4 substantially expands documentation with MoCoDAD optimizer, learning-rate, epoch and diffusion settings; hand-keypoint sources; missing-keypoint handling; and the GPT-4 prompt, manual review and action-category mapping used for analysis. These are newly documented details, not evidence that existing experiments were rerun. Conversely, v3's explicit heatmap sigma of 3.2 disappears, supplementary citations remain unresolved, and code release is still promised rather than provided.

R1.justification: V4 adds PREGO and distinguishes approaches that avoid mistake labels but require action annotations. It adds gaze/psychology references and citations supporting the new supervised baselines, replaces the Salvador–Chan DTW citation with Sakoe, and drops the direct Segment Anything citation. These are targeted changes around the retained central positioning of unsupervised mistake detection through gaze completion.

P1.justification: V4 retitles the paper, changes author information, substantially rewrites the abstract and parts of the introduction, related work and experimental discussion, and reorganizes the experimental sections. Existing implementation explanations and gaze-estimation material move into a newly structured supplement, while applicability analysis becomes a main-text section.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is rearranged into a single-column display, Figure 2 loses the sum-fusion path, and the benchmark tables gain substantial comparison blocks. The scoring illustration and gaze-estimation table move to the supplement. New statistical plots, category tables, a threshold curve and sequence-based heatmap comparisons replace or extend earlier displays. The IndustReal table also reverses its precision/recall headers.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially strengthens v3's limited comparative foundation by adding hand-based anomaly-detection controls and supervised reference models, while category-level and sensitivity analyses make the method's usefulness more assessable. This improves the empirical argument despite unchanged headline results for the principal model. Unresolved supplementary citations, contradictory confidence prose, a misattributed category result and removal of the key-step-ordering limitation detract from the revision, but the stronger comparative evidence provides a substantial net benefit.
